Tidal barrier upgrade approved

By Sam Example

The regional council on Monday approved a long-planned upgrade to the estuary tidal barrier, ending a two-year debate over cost and design. The works will raise the barrier gates by forty centimetres and replace the ageing hydraulic system that operators say has become unreliable during winter storms.

Engineers told the council that the current gates were designed for sea levels observed in the nineteen-seventies. Recent surge events have come within a few centimetres of overtopping the structure, and the insurance costs for properties along the lower river have risen sharply as a result.

Construction is expected to begin next spring and to take roughly eighteen months. During that period the barrier will remain operational, with temporary pumps installed on the northern bank to handle high-water events while each gate is replaced in turn.

Residents' groups welcomed the decision but asked for a clearer timetable on the road closures the project will require. The council said a detailed schedule would be published before the end of the year, alongside a consultation on noise limits for night work.
